Notes.Text: These are all security issues fixed in the valkey-9.2.0-1.1 package on the GA media of openSUSE Tumbleweed.

Vulnerabilities.Description: In Valkey before 7.2.16, 8.0.x before 8.0.13, 8.1.x before 8.1.12, 9.0.x before 9.0.8, 9.1.x before 9.1.4 and 9.2.0 release candidates, when client eviction is enabled (maxmemory-clients is not 0), an authenticated user who can write to a key that other clients are blocked on (for example with BLPOP, BLMPOP, BZPOPMIN or XREAD BLOCK) can trigger a use-after-free. While the clients blocked on that key are served, evictClients() can select and free the client whose command made the key ready, although that command is still executing, and the server then keeps using the freed client. The blocked clients do not have to belong to the attacker. The result is a reliable crash of the server process. Servers with the default maxmemory-clients 0 are not affected.
